Article 7
(1) Every Woman has the right to:
a. live peacefully, safely, in peace, happily, prosperously physically and spiritually,
b. live in a family within the bond of a legal marriage; c. maintain life and improve her standard of living; d. have work that she likes and is also entitled to fair employment conditions;
e. obtain education and teaching in all types, levels and pathways of education in accordance with the requirements determined;
f. a healthy and clean environment;
g. receive fair wages in accordance with her work that is comparable and commensurate with human dignity,
h. elect and/or be elected in general elections, regional head elections, village head elections and/or other political office elections based on equal rights through direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair voting according to applicable laws and regulations;
i. obtain special protection specifically in the implementation of her work or profession against matters that may threaten safety and/or health related to women's reproductive function; and
j. special rights inherent to women due to their reproductive function are guaranteed and protected by law.
(2) Women who are adults and or are married have the right to perform legal acts independently unless otherwise determined by laws and regulations and other social norms.
-6- (3) A legal marriage can only take place based on the free will of the woman and the man in accordance with laws and regulations.
(4) A wife during the marriage bond has the same rights and responsibilities as her husband over all matters relating to her married life, relations with her children and ownership rights and management of joint property.
(5) After the dissolution of her marriage a woman has the same rights and responsibilities as her former husband over all matters relating to her children, taking into account the best interests of the child.
(6) After the dissolution of marriage, a woman has the same rights as her former husband over all matters relating to joint property without reducing the rights of children, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(7) Every woman who is in a condition of Disability, elderly age, and pregnant is entitled to obtain facilities and special treatment.
(8) Every elderly woman, with physical and/or mental disability, has the right to obtain care, education, training and special assistance at the expense of the regional government to ensure a decent life in accordance with human dignity.

1.5.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, “kekerasan” is defined narrowly as unlawful acts against physical and psychological integrity that endanger life/body or deprive liberty (Pasal 1 angka 10). The regulation discusses services (including “pelayanan kemandirian ekonomi” in Pasal 11(1)(e)) and broader women’s economic rights (Pasal 7), but it does not explicitly recognize “kekerasan ekonomi” (economic violence), economic neglect, or economic exploitation as a form/type of violence. Because the document frames economic aspects as empowerment/assistance rather than defining them as violence, a ‘No’ judgment is consistent with the source text; thus the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-interprets the presence of economic services as coverage of economic violence.

Pasal 9 ayat (1) huruf b states: “melakukan pendidikan tentang nilai-nilai anti kekerasan terhadap perempuan” (conduct education about anti-violence values toward women). This is direct primary-prevention-through-education language. Therefore the predicted ‘Yes’ matches the source text, and the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.

CHAPTER X
MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING
Article 27
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection in the Region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically starting from planning up to the policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection for the current year.
(4) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(5) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.
(6) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of integrated services for the Protection of women victims of violence to the Governor with a copy submitted to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs, and the minister in charge of home affairs.
(7) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of the establishment and development of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions in an integrated manner to the minister in charge of home affairs with a copy to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(8) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) and paragraph (7) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

7.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text in Pasal 26(2) states: “Dalam hal Daerah mendapatkan bantuan pendanaan ... dari Pemerintah wajib dilaksanakan sesuai dengan peraturan perundang-undangan.” Pasal 1 angka 1 defines “Pemerintah” as “Pemerintah Pusat” (Central Government). This explicitly contemplates national/central government funding assistance as a possible funding source (even if conditional on receiving it). Thus the judge’s ‘Yes’ is supported by the source text, and the golden label ‘No’ appears wrong.
